about: Hollerhorn Distilling sits on a hillside outside Naples, the old grape village at the south end of Canandaigua Lake. Karl Neubauer, a Naples native and longtime custom home builder, studied distilling for some fifteen years before he and his wife Melissa opened in 2018, in a building Karl framed from timber salvaged out of collapsing barns. A fire in May 2022 destroyed the tasting room, but the production room and dozens of barrels survived behind a firewall, and the couple rebuilt with help from the whole valley.

This bourbon starts with New York distilling grains, including heirloom open-pollinated corn grown in the Finger Lakes. It is fermented and distilled on site in Naples and aged in new charred oak, as bourbon requires. Every bottle comes from one barrel, so proof and character shift a little from cask to cask; Karl works almost entirely with ingredients from within forty miles of the distillery, so the grain itself changes with each year’s harvest. Hollerhorn describes its single barrel bourbon as full-bodied and oily, with brown sugar, caramel, burnt orange and vanilla. Eden pours a six-year-old barrel, one of the older whiskeys a distillery founded in 2018 can offer.
facts: New York grains with heirloom open-pollinated Finger Lakes corn (at least 51% corn)
Fermented and distilled in Naples, NY
Single barrel, proof varies by barrel (one release 47.3% ABV)
title: Hollerhorn Distilling Single Barrel Bourbon
